import pandas as pd

# File paths for source data
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/training_1.csv"
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/target_multisource_cot.csv"

# Step 1: Load Source 0
# Schema: ['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
# Load with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Step 2: Load Source 1
# Schema: ['item_id', 'movie title', 'release date', 'video release date', 'IMDb URL', ...]
# We only need 'item_id' and 'movie title' columns for the target
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0, usecols=['item_id', 'movie title'])

# Step 3: Join Source 0 and Source 1 on 'item_id'
# This will add the 'movie title' column to the ratings data
df_merged = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1, on='item_id', how='inner')

# Step 4: Ensure target schema and types
# Target schema: ['user_id': int, 'item_id': int, 'rating': int, 'timestamp': int, 'movie title': str]
df_merged = df_merged.astype({
    'user_id': 'int64',
    'item_id': 'int64',
    'rating': 'int64',
    'timestamp': 'int64',
    'movie title': 'string'
})

# Step 5: Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_target = df_merged[['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'movie title']]

# Step 6: Save the result to the specified output path
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
